_doc: Doctor Who — sixty years of planets, most of them visited once and never mentioned again. That is the point of the show and the reason it belongs here: nowhere else offers a diamond planet, a library the size of a world, and a town called Christmas.

destinations.name: Skaro
destinations.blurb: A petrified jungle and a glass desert left by a thousand-year war, with a domed city below and the surviving Kaleds rebuilt as something with no capacity for pity.

destinations.name: Trenzalore
destinations.blurb: A snowbound town called Christmas where nobody can tell a lie, kept in permanent siege by every enemy the Doctor ever made, and rather lovely between attacks.

destinations.name: Midnight
destinations.blurb: A planet of solid diamond under a sun whose light kills anything it touches, viewed from sealed leisure buses. Objectively spectacular, and something out there learns to speak by copying you.

destinations.name: The Library
destinations.blurb: An entire planet built as a library, holding every book ever written, with a moon that stops the pages rotting. Silent for a hundred years, and the shadows on the floor are not all shadows.

destinations.name: Apalapucia
destinations.blurb: Voted the second most beautiful planet in the galaxy — glorious silver colonnades, two suns, and a quarantine facility where a lifetime passes in a day so the dying can be visited without catching it.

destinations.name: The Rings of Akhaten
destinations.blurb: Seven worlds orbiting one star, where a pyramid holds something old and hungry and the entrance fee is a song. Payment everywhere is sentimental: rings, keepsakes, things you cannot bear to lose.

destinations.name: New Earth
destinations.blurb: Humanity's replacement Earth, five billion years on, with apple grass on the hills above New New York — the fifteenth city of that name, and nobody counts the first fourteen.

destinations.name: Malcassairo
destinations.blurb: The last planet, a hundred trillion years on, where the stars have gone out and the last humans queue for a rocket to somewhere called Utopia that may not be there.

destinations.name: Karn
destinations.blurb: A volcanic world of black rock and a Sacred Flame tended by the Sisterhood, whose Elixir of Life will fix anything, at a price, and whose ship-wrecking mind-powers explain the debris field.

destinations.name: Peladon
destinations.blurb: A cold mountain kingdom of superstition and mining strikes, arguing itself into the Galactic Federation while a sacred beast called Aggedor may or may not still stalk the tunnels.

destinations.name: Androzani Minor
destinations.blurb: A hollow, unstable moon of mud bursts and gun-runners, where raw spectrox — the most valuable substance in existence, and lethal before refining — is scraped out of the caves.

destinations.name: Bowie Base One, Mars
destinations.blurb: The first human colony on Mars, a tidy dome of hydroponics and glaciers, on the specific day in 2059 that history records everyone dying. The view is exceptional.

destinations.name: Telos
destinations.blurb: An ice world whose original inhabitants were displaced by the Cybermen, who built vast refrigerated tombs beneath the surface and lay down in them to wait for somebody curious.

destinations.name: Demons Run
destinations.blurb: A military asteroid base run by an order of fighting clerics, built around the belief that demons run when a good man goes to war. Impressively fortified, currently between occupants.
tags: a good man goes to war

destinations.name: Darillium
destinations.blurb: Home to the Singing Towers, which sing, and a restaurant with a twenty-four-year night where couples go to say the things they have been putting off. Bring tissues.

destinations.name: Villengard
destinations.blurb: Once the galaxy's largest weapons factory, now a banana grove, following an incident the Doctor declines to elaborate on. Bananas are good; you should always bring a banana to a party.

destinations.name: Terra Alpha
destinations.blurb: A human colony where unhappiness is a capital offence, enforced by women in pink and a robot made of confectionery. Everyone smiles. The disappearances are not discussed.

destinations.name: San Helios
destinations.blurb: A city of a hundred billion, reduced to a desert in a single year by a swarm that eats worlds and moves on through a wormhole. The sand is what is left of the city.

destinations.name: Vortis
destinations.blurb: An airless world of acid pools and volcanic craters, webbed over by something malevolent, and home to the Menoptra — a civilisation of enormous, courteous butterflies.

destinations.name: Logopolis
destinations.blurb: A quiet stone city where mathematicians mutter numbers that hold the universe together. Do not interrupt them, do not raise your voice, and do not touch anything.
